videos.script: Three providers so far: OpenAI, Google and Cohere. The market is wider than that, and this lesson walks the rest of it. {{market}} It starts with Jina. Jina's endpoint copies OpenAI's shape, so a plain HTTP client is enough. One extra field matters. It is called task, and it tells the model whether the text is a question or the passage that answers it. {{jina}} Then the price sheet. Voyage and Mistral are on it. So are models for code and for law, and open models that a hosting company sells by the token. Jina is not on it, and the lesson says so instead of guessing. {{sheet}} Then a different kind of model altogether. A static model is a table with one row per word piece. It has no layers to run. On this machine it embeds a hundred and fifty messages more than a hundred times faster than MiniLM. {{speed}} You will see where that speed costs you, ticket by ticket. {{misses}} Then the rule that makes changing models expensive. Vectors from two models never mix, even with the same number of dimensions. {{switch}} You will plan a migration that never mixes them. And you will finish with a way to choose: rule out by language, privacy and licence first, then measure what survives on your own questions. {{choose}}
